field_name: Temporal Retrieval for Evolving Documents in Question Answering

categories.name: Temporal Decay Analysis in Legal/Statutory Context
categories.description: Studies measuring temporal degradation of retrieval signals in legal statutes over time, often using citation proxies.

categories.name: Temporal Weighting Applications in Other Modalities
categories.description: Application of temporal decay or weighting to video retrieval, recommendation systems, and knowledge graphs.

categories.name: Open-Domain QA Retrieval Efficiency
categories.description: Work focused on improving retrieval efficiency (speed/accuracy trade-off) for open-domain question answering, without explicit temporal handling.

categories.name: Preference Optimization / LLM Alignment with Temporal Decay
categories.description: Incorporating temporal decay into preference optimization methods for aligning large language models with human feedback.

categories.name: Temporal Relevance Weighting for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering over Evolving Regulatory Texts
categories.description: Proposed approach: retrieval-agnostic framework adding temporal relevance component based on version timestamps to improve QA over continuously amended documents.

idea_position: Temporal Relevance Weighting for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering over Evolving Regulatory Texts
common_assumptions: Temporal proximity between document version timestamp and query target date correlates with relevance.
Standard retriever provides a semantic similarity score that can be combined with temporal weight.
Version timestamps are available or can be inferred from document metadata.
Answer accuracy can be measured using standard QA metrics (Exact Match, F1).

repeated_limitations.description: Evaluation is a proxy (e.g., citation prediction) rather than end-user question answering.
Focuses on a specific modality (video, recommendation, knowledge graphs) not textual document retrieval or QA.
Limited to a specific language or domain (e.g., Korean QA, Ukrainian legal system).
Does not address evolving document collections or versioned texts.
Does not propose or test mitigation strategies for temporal decay.

underexplored_combinations: Temporal relevance weighting combined with dense retrievers (e.g., ColBERT, DPR) for open-domain QA over versioned regulatory texts.
Hybrid graph-text temporal retrieval approaches for legal statutes (combining co-citation signals with textual relevance and temporal weighting).
Benchmark construction for temporal QA using publicly available versioned regulatory corpora (e.g., US Code, Federal Regulations, international equivalents) with time-stamped queries.
Evaluation of temporal relevance component using end-to-end QA pipelines (retriever + reader) rather than retrieval-only metrics.

contradictions.description: Some works find uniform temporal decay performs poorly compared to no temporal weighting (arxiv:2604.26970), while others apply uniform temporal decay weighting with positive results in recommendation (doi:10.33480/jitk.v12i1.8240) - suggesting effectiveness may depend on domain and signal type.
